Title: Enhancing credit scoring with alternative data
Authors or Organisation: Viani Biatat Djeundje; Jonathan Crook; Raffaella Calabrese; Mona Hamid
Method or Data: Microcredit application data; demographic, psychometric, email and other alternative variables; multiple predictive models
Key Contribution: Provides direct empirical evidence that alternative data can improve or substitute for conventional data; one data ensemble originated from a Nigerian bank
Main Limitation: Does not provide a Nigeria-wide data architecture, production deployment, fairness governance, or MLOps lifecycle
Relevance to Proposed Framework: Closest empirical precedent using Nigerian-origin borrower data; use to justify alternative-data experiments and model comparison
Access: Publisher page; author manuscript may be available
Status or Notes: Read methods, dataset construction, validation design, results and limitations in full

Title: FairLend-Africa: An Explainable Machine Learning Framework for Alternative Credit Scoring Using Behavioral Financial Data in Financially Excluded African Communities
Primary Theme: Alternative data; XAI; fairness; financial inclusion
Method or Data: Synthetic dataset of 10,000 records; XGBoost and logistic regression; SHAP; fairness audit; REST API and dashboard
Key Contribution: Demonstrates an integrated African-oriented prototype with explainability, fairness analysis and deployable interfaces
Main Limitation: Synthetic data; SSRN preprint; conclusions require validation on real borrowers and lender operations
Relevance to Proposed Framework: Very close system precedent; distinguish the proposed work through real Nigerian data, stronger governance, temporal validation and MLOps
Access: Open abstract; paper available from SSRN
Status or Notes: Treat as a recent non-peer-reviewed precedent, not definitive evidence

Title: PDx: Adaptive Credit Risk Forecasting Model in Digital Lending using Machine Learning Operations
Authors or Organisation: Sultan Amed; Chan Yu Hang; Sayantan Banerjee
Primary Theme: MLOps; probability of default; model monitoring
Method or Data: Three credit datasets; champion-challenger modelling; out-of-time validation; monitoring and retraining pipeline
Key Contribution: Shows how MLOps can manage credit-model degradation, drift, retraining, reproducibility and production governance
Main Limitation: Not designed for Nigeria and does not centre alternative-data inclusion or Nigerian regulation
Relevance to Proposed Framework: Primary technical precedent for the proposed monitoring, retraining and champion-challenger architecture
Status or Notes: Read architecture, target definitions, temporal tests and retraining triggers

Title: Artificial intelligence and credit risk assessment in Nigeria's digital lending market: an econometric analysis
Primary Theme: AI adoption; digital lending; default risk; regulation
Method or Data: Simulated panel data representing fintech operations from 2017 to 2025; logistic regression and panel OLS
Key Contribution: Connects AI and alternative-data adoption to credit performance and governance in the Nigerian digital-lending context
Main Limitation: Relies on simulated data and an econometric adoption analysis rather than an implemented borrower-level scoring platform
Relevance to Proposed Framework: Useful contextual evidence, but the proposed study should make stronger empirical and engineering contributions
Status or Notes: Scrutinise simulation assumptions and do not treat simulated effects as observed lender outcomes

Title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Enhancing Financial Inclusion in Microfinance Lending in Nigeria
Authors or Organisation: Saidu Halidu Ibrahim; Abdullahi Usman Ya'u; Amina Umar Ahmed
Method or Data: Sequential explanatory mixed methods; survey of 720 microfinance stakeholders and 15 interviews
Key Contribution: Documents adoption patterns, perceived value and implementation barriers in Nigerian microfinance
Main Limitation: Stakeholder perceptions rather than borrower-level default modelling; no deployable scoring pipeline
Relevance to Proposed Framework: Supports institutional-adoption analysis and requirements for microfinance users of the framework
Status or Notes: Use for adoption barriers and stakeholder context, not model-performance claims

Title: AI for women's financial inclusion: analysis of product design and policy approaches in Nigeria
Primary Theme: Gender inclusion; AI policy; responsible design
Method or Data: Qualitative analysis of public data and Nigerian fintech services
Key Contribution: Shows that technology alone does not ensure inclusion and highlights gender bias, access, affordability, appropriateness and sustainability
Main Limitation: Not an empirical credit-scoring experiment and does not build a model
Relevance to Proposed Framework: Important source for subgroup fairness, gender-disaggregated evaluation and inclusion outcomes
Status or Notes: Use to prevent the project from equating model availability with genuine inclusion

Title: Use of Machine Learning Techniques to Create a Credit Score Model for Airtime Loans
Authors or Organisation: Bernard Dushimimana; Yvonne Wambui; Timothy Lubega; Patrick E. McSharry
Method or Data: More than 3 million loans and over 41,000 customers; logistic regression, decision trees and random forest
Key Contribution: Demonstrates large-scale behavioural credit modelling and evaluates business profitability as well as classification performance
Main Limitation: Product- and market-specific; limited demographic fairness evidence; no general Nigerian adoption framework
Relevance to Proposed Framework: Strong methodological example for behavioural data, rare-event defaults and financial-value evaluation
Status or Notes: Read target window, leakage controls, cross-validation and profit analysis carefully

Title: Who gets the money? A qualitative analysis of fintech lending and credit scoring through the adoption of AI and alternative data
Authors or Organisation: Maximilian Tigges; Sonke Mestwerdt; Sebastian Tschirner; Rene Mauer
Method or Data: Gioia qualitative method; interviews with 26 experts
Key Contribution: Synthesises benefits for risk management and inclusion alongside consent, bias, privacy, traceability and accountability risks
Main Limitation: Qualitative and not Nigeria-specific; does not validate predictive models
Relevance to Proposed Framework: Useful global best-practice and responsible-AI foundation for governance requirements
Access: Publisher page; may require institutional access
Status or Notes: Code its governance themes into system requirements

Title: Machine learning powered financial credit scoring: a systematic literature review
Primary Theme: ML credit scoring; alternative data; explainability
Method or Data: Systematic synthesis of machine-learning credit-scoring studies
Key Contribution: Identifies recurring gaps in standardised datasets, evaluation, interpretability, privacy, fairness and real-world implementation
Main Limitation: Broad review; conclusions may not capture all Nigerian market and regulatory conditions
Relevance to Proposed Framework: Use to structure the formal literature review and demonstrate where the integrated framework contributes
Status or Notes: Use its search strategy and references to expand the final corpus

Title: How do machine learning and non-traditional data affect credit scoring? New evidence from a Chinese fintech firm
Authors or Organisation: Leonardo Gambacorta; Yiping Huang; Han Qiu; Jingyi Wang
Method or Data: Proprietary transaction-level fintech data; comparison of ML and traditional models under normal conditions and a credit-supply shock
Key Contribution: Finds that ML with non-traditional data can improve loss/default prediction, particularly under stress, while the advantage falls for borrowers with longer histories
Main Limitation: Different regulatory and market context; proprietary model details may be limited
Relevance to Proposed Framework: Global benchmark for testing robustness under economic shifts and thin-file versus thick-file segments
Status or Notes: Use for stress testing and borrower-history segmentation

Title: Financial Inclusion and National Financial Inclusion Strategy resources
Primary Theme: Financial inclusion policy; targets; enabling infrastructure
Method or Data: Official strategy documents and policy resources
Key Contribution: Defines Nigeria's policy objectives, access dimensions, target populations and institutional context
Main Limitation: Policy goals are not evidence that targets were achieved; individual documents have different dates
Relevance to Proposed Framework: Grounds the problem statement, adoption environment and inclusion outcome measures
Status or Notes: Use the latest available strategy document and record its publication date

Title: Access to Financial Services in Nigeria 2023 Survey
Primary Theme: Financial inclusion; consumer behaviour; underserved groups
Method or Data: Nationwide demand-side survey covering more than 20,000 consumers; dataset available by proposal
Key Contribution: Provides recent Nigerian evidence on formal inclusion, exclusion, product usage and consumer financial lives
Main Limitation: Cross-sectional inclusion survey; not a labelled loan-default dataset
Relevance to Proposed Framework: Supports population context, segment design and possible non-default inclusion analyses
Access: Open reports; microdata requires a request to EFInA
Status or Notes: Request the dataset with a short academic research proposal if individual-level analysis is needed

Title: Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023
Authors or Organisation: Federal Republic of Nigeria; Nigeria Data Protection Commission
Primary Theme: Privacy; lawful processing; data-subject rights; governance
Key Contribution: Establishes the legal framework governing personal-data processing and the NDPC
Main Limitation: Legal interpretation requires qualified review; implementing guidance may evolve
Relevance to Proposed Framework: Must inform consent, data minimisation, sensitive/proxy features, retention, security, DPIA and automated-decision governance
Status or Notes: Use the Act itself rather than summaries; verify current NDPC guidance before final design

Title: Digital, Electronic, Online, or Non-Traditional Consumer Lending Regulations 2025 and Guidelines
Authors or Organisation: Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission
Primary Theme: Digital lending; consumer protection; transparency; responsible conduct
Key Contribution: Provides a detailed reference for digital-lending registration, disclosure, privacy, redress and responsible conduct
Main Limitation: Implementation and enforcement were reported suspended by a Federal High Court order in May 2026; legal status may change
Relevance to Proposed Framework: Relevant to adoption controls, but every legal claim must state and verify the current enforcement status
Status or Notes: Do not describe as fully enforceable without checking the latest court and FCCPC update

Title: WASPAN v. FCCPC: notice suspending implementation and enforcement of the DEON Regulations 2025
Authors or Organisation: Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission
Method or Data: Official FCCPC notice concerning Federal High Court proceedings
Key Contribution: Records that FCCPC suspended implementation and enforcement in response to an April 2026 ex-parte order
Main Limitation: Procedural status may change after the date of the notice
Relevance to Proposed Framework: Prevents the research from presenting the 2025 DEON rules as unquestionably active; supports a current-law verification step
Status or Notes: Recheck before proposal submission, ethics review, pilot design and publication

Title: Nigeria: Global Financial Inclusion (Global Findex) Database 2021
Method or Data: Country microdata, questionnaire, codebook and global report; DOI-indexed dataset
Key Contribution: Provides internationally comparable inclusion indicators and individual-level Nigerian survey data
Main Limitation: Not a loan-performance dataset and predates recent Nigerian market developments
Relevance to Proposed Framework: Useful for international comparison, descriptive analysis and underserved-population profiling
Status or Notes: Use survey weights and codebook; do not derive default-risk labels from inclusion indicators

Title: The Global Findex Database 2021: Financial Inclusion, Digital Payments, and Resilience in the Age of COVID-19
Authors or Organisation: Asli Demirguc-Kunt; Leora Klapper; Dorothe Singer; Saniya Ansar; World Bank
Method or Data: Global representative survey report and database
Key Contribution: Supplies global benchmarks and definitions for inclusion, account ownership, payments, saving and borrowing
Main Limitation: Latest full global wave listed here is 2021; country conditions may have changed
Relevance to Proposed Framework: Provides the global comparison required by the phrase 'adapting global best practices'
Status or Notes: Use alongside the Nigeria-specific Findex microdata and EFInA 2023

Title: The Use of Alternative Data in Credit Risk Assessment
Primary Theme: Alternative data; credit infrastructure; consumer protection
Method or Data: Policy and industry evidence review with implementation examples
Key Contribution: Summarises adoption models, data categories, benefits, partnerships and associated risks
Relevance to Proposed Framework: Useful for data-source selection, lender partnerships, safeguards and global practice comparisons
Status or Notes: Extract an evidence table of data types, benefits, risks and governance safeguards
